description:
verify_responder_is_delegated_by (pkix-chain/src/lib.rs lines 1328-1379) checks BOTH DN equality AND cryptographic signature binding for the RFC 6960 §4.2.2.2 responder delegation. The cryptographic half (verifying the responder cert's signature under the supplied issuer's SPKI) is non-obvious: a naive reading of RFC 6960 §4.2.2.2 'This certificate MUST be issued directly by the CA that is identified in the request' could be read as a DN-equality check.

WHY THIS IS CORRECT: in cross-signed CA topologies, two distinct CAs can share an issuer DN (an intermediate cross-signed by two roots; an enterprise CA with a name collision). An attacker who controls EITHER such CA can mint a responder cert that DN-matches the legitimate issuer. DN equality alone admits this attack — see the test verify_ocsp_responder_twin_dn_issuer_returns_ocsp_delegation in tests/verify_ocsp_responder.rs.

WHAT A FUTURE CONTRIBUTOR MIGHT WRONGLY SUGGEST: 'the chain validation already verified chain[0] is signed by chain[1] / anchor, so the DN check on issuer.subject is sufficient — we don't need a separate signature op.' That suggestion misses the distinction: chain validation proves chain[0] is signed by SOME issuer trusted by the path; the wrapper's delegation check proves chain[0] is signed by the SPECIFIC issuer the caller named. Two different statements; the second cannot be derived from the first when the path has alternative roots.

CHANGELOG entry: 'Fixed - OCSP responder delegation: cryptographic binding now enforced.'

The test corpus (root-twin-dn.der) was generated by gen.py (pyca/cryptography oracle, line 339-378) and exercises exactly the DN-twin attack the binding check defends against.

DEFEND IF: someone suggests dropping the cryptographic check 'because the chain already validated' or merging the binding check with the chain walk 'to avoid the extra signature op.' Both suggestions break the security property.
title: OCSP delegation cryptographic binding fix (PKIX-q9hv.3) — defend against dropping DN-twin protection
